ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Which bird is adapted for clinging to and climbing trees?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a group of schematic diagrams of bird heads and bird beaks labeled with letters. The shapes of the bird beaks are different; among them, the bird head labeled G has a short, straight, sturdy, sharp chisel-like beak, suitable for pecking or drilling into tree bark. Reasoning: The question asks which kind of bird is adapted to tightly grasp and climb trees. The bird that has this kind of chisel-like beak and is characterized typically by pecking wood and climbing tree trunks is the woodpecker; woodpeckers also have adaptations such as feet suitable for clinging to tree trunks and stiff tail feathers. Therefore the answer is Woodpecker.
